en.name: Teff flour
en.summary: Teff flour keeps 2 months in the pantry and 4 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Teff grains are too small to hull, so the flour is always wholegrain — bran, germ, oil and all — which is why the window is short.
en.pantry: 2 months in an airtight container on a cool, dark, dry shelf. Teff is the smallest cultivated grain in the world, far too small to separate into bran and endosperm, so every teff flour is a wholegrain flour whether the bag says so or not. That means the germ oil is always in there, and oil oxidises. Fresh teff smells faintly sweet, malty and a little like cocoa; a stale bag smells sharp and tastes bitter, which shows up plainly in injera, where the only other flavour is the ferment.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for teff flour. Cold storage slows the oil and is worth considering for a bag you use occasionally, but only in a genuinely airtight container — teff is a very fine flour and takes up moisture and fridge odours quickly, and a cold bag opened in a warm kitchen condenses water into itself. Between the two, the freezer is the better use of the space.
en.freezer: 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F), the sensible default unless you make injera regularly. Use an airtight tub or a double bag with the air pressed out, and label it. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that; what runs out is flavour as the oil oxidises slowly even cold. Let the sealed container come up to room temperature before opening, and let the flour warm before you start a batter — a teff ferment started with cold flour is slow to get going.
en.thawing: Bring the sealed container to room temperature before opening so the flour does not take up condensation, and let it warm before mixing a fermented batter.
spoilage: A sharp or paint-like smell instead of a faintly malty, cocoa-ish one.
Bitterness in the injera, where there is nothing else to mask it.
Clumping or hard lumps, meaning moisture reached the flour.
Webbing, larvae or small moths in the container.
tips: Buy small bags unless you make injera often.
Store in an opaque airtight tub, not the bag it came in.
Smell before starting a ferment; rancid flour makes bitter injera.
Ivory and brown teff store the same way — the difference is flavour, not keeping quality.

faq.q: How long does teff flour last?
faq.a: 2 months in an airtight container in the pantry, or 4 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Why is teff flour always wholegrain?
faq.a: The grain is too small to hull, so bran and germ cannot be separated out. That is also why it carries oil and keeps for a shorter time than white flour.
Yes, 4 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Seal it airtight and let it come back to room temperature before opening or mixing a batter.

zh.name: 苔麩粉
zh.summary: 苔麩粉密封放常溫可放 2 個月，−18 °C 冷凍是 4 個月。苔麩的顆粒太小，根本沒辦法脫殼，所以所有苔麩粉都是全穀粉——麩皮、胚芽、油脂全都在裡面，這就是期限短的原因。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐、放陰涼避光乾燥的架子，2 個月。苔麩是全世界最小的栽培穀物，小到無法把麩皮和胚乳分開，所以不管包裝上寫不寫，每一種苔麩粉都是全穀粉。這代表胚芽油永遠在裡面，而油會氧化。新鮮苔麩粉聞起來微甜、帶麥芽香，甚至有一點可可味；走味的一袋則刺鼻、吃起來發苦，而在英傑拉裡除了發酵味之外沒有別的味道可以遮，那股苦會非常明顯。
zh.fridge: 苔麩粉沒有公布的冷藏期限。低溫能拖慢油脂，對偶爾才用的份量值得考慮，但一定要用真正密封的容器——苔麩粉極細，吸濕和吸味都很快，一包冰過的粉在溫暖廚房裡打開就會自己結露。兩者之間，把空間留給冷凍更划算。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 4 個月；除非你經常做英傑拉，否則這就是合理的預設。用密封罐或套兩層袋、壓出空氣，並貼標籤。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；先用完的是風味，因為油脂在低溫下仍會慢慢氧化。開蓋前先讓整罐回到室溫；調發酵麵糊前也讓粉回溫——用冰冷的粉起發酵，會起得很慢。
zh.thawing: 整罐密封著回到室溫再開蓋，粉才不會受潮；調發酵麵糊前也先讓它回溫。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻或帶油漆味，而不是微微的麥芽與可可香。
做出來的英傑拉發苦——那裡沒有別的味道遮得住。
結塊或出現硬塊，表示水氣碰到粉了。
容器裡出現絲網、幼蟲或小蛾。
tips: 除非常做英傑拉，否則買小包就好。
用不透光的密封罐，不要就著原袋放。
起發酵之前先聞一下；油耗的粉會做出苦的英傑拉。
白苔麩和褐苔麩的保存方式一樣，差別在風味，不在耐放程度。

faq.a: 密封放常溫 2 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 4 個月。

faq.q: 苔麩粉為什麼一定是全穀粉？
faq.a: 顆粒太小，沒辦法把麩皮和胚芽分出來。這也是它帶油、比白麵粉更不耐放的原因。
可以，−18 °C 下 4 個月。密封好，開蓋和調麵糊前都先讓它回到室溫。
